## Provider usage and latency

The frozen 61-case predictions reference 3,911 Jev decisions: 13,842,402 input tokens, 806,338 output tokens, and $0.581380884 of provider-reported decision cost. Semantic-prior acquisition retained 27,858,287 embedding input tokens; the provider returned no embedding cost field. Full retained-evidence and operational timing details are in [USAGE.md](USAGE.md). Provider request latency was not present in the frozen envelopes and is not invented from replay time.

## Interpretation and limitations

Iteration 013 is a frozen selector over Atlas, not Atlas itself. The structural oracle measures whether the finite Atlas family contains a better state; it uses evaluator gold and cannot be deployed. Repository differences, selector failures, and precision/recall/context tradeoffs must therefore be read separately. The study covers the frozen JS/TS subset and does not establish a matched full-benchmark leaderboard rank or an end-to-end coding-agent speedup.

The 15 historical-development cases influenced policy development and are not pooled into the untouched validation estimate. Later Atlas signature analysis may explore relationships between repository geometry and these localization regimes, but that analysis is post hoc and will not retune this result.
